key_insight: Noisy module-to-module links can support fault-tolerant logical operations in modular quantum computers, with only a modest impact on surface-code thresholds.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that distributed QPUs can scale quantum error correction without requiring ultra-clean interfaces, while also reducing the resource cost of preparing multi-module entangled states.
method: Simulated fault-tolerant nonlocal CNOT gates using lattice surgery between rotated surface-code QPUs connected by noisy Bell pairs.
Analyzed logical error rates under both interface noise and intra-QPU noise.
Developed a low-overhead distributed GHZ-state preparation protocol and framed ancilla minimization as a vertex-cover problem with a polynomial-time heuristic.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations in the abstract indicate that interfaces can tolerate noise roughly an order of magnitude higher than internal QPU noise with only a small threshold reduction.
watch_item: The heuristic lowers overhead, but real hardware performance will still depend on how reliably noisy Bell-pair interfaces and inter-module synchronization can be implemented.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Logical Operations and Efficient State Preparation in Modular Quantum Architectures with Noisy Interfaces
